doc.title: Roy Haynes — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Where jazz and drumming are heading; his current band
summary: His band is Kikoski, Burno and Harrison or Braden; great young drummers abound but the music is drifting toward swingless and synthetic.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Where are you going now? I know you’re doing your own projects. Who’s in your band now?

Good question. Kikoski. My next gig is in Texas. Dave Kikoski will be there. Dwayne Burno will be on bass. And Donald Harrison – no. Donald’s making my summer tour on alto, but Don Braden’s going to play tenor with us for this Texas.
What do you think about the direction of jazz now and drumming in particular?

They got a lot of great drummers out there, great young drummers coming up. They got a lot of great younger musicians coming up, but the direction of a lot of the music – it’s going different directions.
You’re saying a lot of drummers are not swinging, maybe?

I say that? I didn’t say that just now. I said that earlier. There are a lot of – there are great drummers, but I’ve heard music where they say, this is not supposed to swing, or that. I have. So they don’t have to swing if they don’t care to. Maybe that’s the direction it’s going. Swingless.
What about the direction that drumming took – you were talking about Trane. He had that internal heart.
I love it. For myself, I love it. You can’t beat it. But things are getting a little more synthetic and going other directions.
